component.name: vertx-websocket
component.title: Vert.x WebSocket
component.description: Receive and send WebSocket messages with Vert.x, as a WebSocket server or as a client of a remote WebSocket server.
component.label: http,networking

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

synchronous.label: consumer
synchronous.description: Whether the consumers route each message synchronously, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the synchronous endpoint option.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

allowOriginHeader.label: advanced
allowOriginHeader.description: Whether the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true add an Origin header to the WebSocket handshake request, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the allowOriginHeader endpoint option.

autowiredEnabled.label: advanced
autowiredEnabled.description: Whether autowiring is enabled. This is used for automatic autowiring options (the option must be marked as autowired) by looking up in the registry to find if there is a single instance of matching type, which then gets configured on the component. This can be used for automatic configuring JDBC data sources, JMS connection factories, AWS Clients, etc.

defaultHost.label: advanced
defaultHost.description: The host of an endpoint whose URI has no host, such as vertx-websocket:/chat. The default 0.0.0.0 makes the server consumer bind to all network interfaces.

defaultPort.label: advanced
defaultPort.description: The port of an endpoint whose URI has no port. With the default 0, the server consumer binds to a free port that the operating system picks, and the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect to port 80, or to port 443 with TLS.

originHeaderUrl.label: advanced
originHeaderUrl.description: The value of the Origin header of the WebSocket handshake request, as the default for the endpoints of this component. See the originHeaderUrl endpoint option.

router.label: advanced
router.description: The Vert.x Router that the HTTP servers of the server consumers use, unless the router option of the endpoint is set. The one router serves the HTTP servers of all hosts and ports. If not set, the Router bean of the registry is used when there is exactly one, and otherwise each HTTP server gets a new router.

vertx.label: advanced
vertx.description: To use an existing Vert.x instance instead of creating a new one. If not set, the component uses the Vertx bean of the registry when there is exactly one, and otherwise creates its own instance, which it closes when it stops.

vertxOptions.label: advanced
vertxOptions.description: The VertxOptions of the Vert.x instance that the component creates. Not used when the component uses an existing Vert.x instance, from the vertx option or a Vertx bean of the registry.

useGlobalSslContextParameters.label: security
useGlobalSslContextParameters.description: Whether to use the global SSL context parameters of the CamelContext for each endpoint that the component creates and that has no sslContextParameters. See the sslContextParameters endpoint option.

CamelVertxWebsocket.connectionKey.description: The key of a peer connected to the server consumer. The server consumer sets it to the key of the peer that the exchange comes from, a key that it creates when the peer connects. The producer sends the message to the peer with this key, or to each peer of a comma-separated list of keys, among the peers that are connected on its path to a server consumer of this component with the same host name and port.

CamelVertxWebsocket.sendToAll.label: producer
CamelVertxWebsocket.sendToAll.description: Whether the producer sends the message to all the peers that are connected on its path to a server consumer of this component with the same host name and port. Replaces the sendToAll option of the endpoint for this message.

CamelVertxWebsocket.remoteAddress.label: consumer
CamelVertxWebsocket.remoteAddress.description: The address of the peer that the exchange comes from, as a Vert.x SocketAddress with its host and port. Set by the server consumer.

CamelVertxWebsocket.event.label: consumer
CamelVertxWebsocket.event.description: The event that the exchange comes from: MESSAGE for a received message, and OPEN or CLOSE for a peer that connects or disconnects when fireWebSocketConnectionEvents is true. Set by the server consumer. An exchange with the event ERROR goes to the exception handler of the consumer instead of the route.

consumerOut.description: The message received: a String for a text frame, a byte array for a binary frame. With fireWebSocketConnectionEvents=true, the OPEN event has the Vert.x ServerWebSocket as body and the CLOSE event no body: the CamelVertxWebsocket.event header tells them apart

producerIn.description: A String is sent as a text frame and a byte array as a binary frame; any other body is converted to a String and sent as a text frame, so a stream with binary content must be converted to bytes first, and a Map or a POJO is sent as its toString: marshal it first. No body sends nothing

host.description: The host name or IP address. The server consumer binds its HTTP server to it, and the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect to it. If the URI has no host, the defaultHost option of the component is used.

port.description: The port number. The server consumer binds its HTTP server to it, and with 0 to a free port that the operating system picks. The producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect to it, and with 0 to port 80, or to port 443 when the connection uses TLS. If the URI has no port, the defaultPort option of the component is used.

path.description: The path of the WebSocket. The server consumer accepts WebSocket connections on it: the path can hold parameters such as /chat/{user}, whose values the consumer sets as headers, and can end with * to accept each path that starts with it. The producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect to it. If the URI has no path, / is used.

allowedOriginPattern.label: consumer
allowedOriginPattern.description: A regular expression for the Origin header of the WebSocket handshake requests that the server consumer accepts. A handshake request whose Origin header does not match is rejected with status 403. If not set, the server consumer does not check the Origin header.

connectMessage.label: consumer
connectMessage.description: When consumeAsClient is set to true, a text message to send to the server each time the consumer connects: when it starts and after each reconnect. For example a subscribe request, for a server that only sends messages to a client that asked for them.

consumeAsClient.label: consumer
consumeAsClient.description: Whether the consumer connects as a WebSocket client to the server at the host, port and path, instead of starting a WebSocket server, and routes each text or binary message that the server sends. The consumer fails to start if it cannot connect. When the connection is lost later, it reconnects as set by reconnectInitialDelay, reconnectInterval and maxReconnectAttempts.

fireWebSocketConnectionEvents.label: consumer
fireWebSocketConnectionEvents.description: Whether the server consumer also routes an exchange when a peer connects, with the event OPEN and the Vert.x ServerWebSocket as body, and when a peer disconnects, with the event CLOSE and no body. The CamelVertxWebsocket.event header holds the event. A consumer with consumeAsClient=true does not use it.

maxReconnectAttempts.label: consumer
maxReconnectAttempts.description: The maximum number of failed reconnect attempts of a consumer with consumeAsClient=true, counted again for each loss of the connection. When they are used up, the consumer logs a warning and stays started without a connection. With the default 0, the consumer tries to reconnect without limit.

reconnectInitialDelay.label: consumer
reconnectInitialDelay.description: The delay in milliseconds from the loss of the connection to the first reconnect attempt, for a consumer with consumeAsClient=true. With the default 0, the first attempt is made at once.

reconnectInterval.label: consumer
reconnectInterval.description: The interval in milliseconds between the reconnect attempts of a consumer with consumeAsClient=true. When an attempt is still running at the end of an interval, no other attempt starts until it ends.

synchronous.label: consumer
synchronous.description: Whether the consumer routes each message synchronously. When true, the route runs on a thread of the Vert.x worker pool, which waits until the route is complete, so the size of the worker pool limits how many messages are routed at the same time. When false, the route starts on a worker thread with the asynchronous routing engine, and the worker thread is free as soon as the route continues on another thread (such as an asynchronous producer), so the worker pool no longer limits the messages in flight. Keep it false for a route that calls an asynchronous producer using the same Vert.x (such as vertx-http): with true, such messages can occupy every worker thread while their producers need a worker thread to complete, and then no message completes.

bridgeErrorHandler.label: consumer,advanced
bridgeErrorHandler.description: Allows for bridging the consumer to the Camel routing Error Handler, which mean any exceptions (if possible) occurred while the Camel consumer is trying to pickup incoming messages, or the likes, will now be processed as a message and handled by the routing Error Handler. Important: This is only possible if the 3rd party component allows Camel to be alerted if an exception was thrown. Some components handle this internally only, and therefore bridgeErrorHandler is not possible. In other situations we may improve the Camel component to hook into the 3rd party component and make this possible for future releases. By default the consumer will use the org.apache.camel.spi.ExceptionHandler to deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exceptionHandler.label: consumer,advanced
exceptionHandler.description: To let the consumer use a custom ExceptionHandler. Notice if the option bridgeErrorHandler is enabled then this option is not in use. By default the consumer will deal with exceptions, that will be logged at WARN or ERROR level and ignored.

exchangePattern.label: consumer,advanced
exchangePattern.description: Sets the exchange pattern when the consumer creates an exchange.

parallelProcessing.label: consumer,advanced
parallelProcessing.description: When consumeAsClient is set to true, whether the received messages are routed in parallel, on the threads of the Vert.x worker pool, in any order. By default (false), the messages of the WebSocket are routed one after the other, in the order they are received.

router.label: consumer,advanced
router.description: The Vert.x Router of the HTTP server of the server consumer, for example to serve other HTTP routes on the same server. All consumers on the same host and port share one HTTP server, which uses the router of the consumer that starts first. If not set, the router option of the component is used.

serverOptions.label: consumer,advanced
serverOptions.description: The Vert.x HttpServerOptions of the HTTP server of the server consumer. All consumers on the same host and port share one HTTP server, which uses the options of the consumer that starts first. The server listens on the host and port of the endpoint, not on those of the options.

clientSubProtocols.label: producer
clientSubProtocols.description: A comma-separated list of the WebSocket subprotocols that the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true request in the Sec-WebSocket-Protocol header of the handshake request.

sendToAll.label: producer
sendToAll.description: Whether the producer sends each message to all the peers that are connected on the path of the endpoint to a server consumer of this component with the same host name and port, instead of to a remote WebSocket server. If no peer is connected, the message is not sent. The CamelVertxWebsocket.sendToAll header replaces this option for a message.

clientOptions.label: producer,advanced
clientOptions.description: The Vert.x WebSocketClientOptions of the WebSocket client that the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect with. Its connect timeout also limits how long they wait for the handshake to complete. When sslContextParameters is set, its TLS settings are applied on top of these options.

lazyStartProducer.label: producer,advanced
lazyStartProducer.description: Whether the producer should be started lazy (on the first message). By starting lazy you can use this to allow CamelContext and routes to startup in situations where a producer may otherwise fail during starting and cause the route to fail being started. By deferring this startup to be lazy then the startup failure can be handled during routing messages via Camel's routing error handlers. Beware that when the first message is processed then creating and starting the producer may take a little time and prolong the total processing time of the processing.

headerFilterStrategy.label: advanced
headerFilterStrategy.description: To use a custom HeaderFilterStrategy to filter the query and path parameters of the WebSocket handshake request, which the server consumer sets as headers of each exchange. The producer does not use it.

allowOriginHeader.label: security
allowOriginHeader.description: Whether the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true add an Origin header, derived from the host and port of the server, to the WebSocket handshake request. Set it to false for a server that rejects handshake requests with an Origin header. Not used when originHeaderUrl is set, as that Origin is always sent.

handshakeHeaders.label: security
handshakeHeaders.description: The HTTP headers to add to the WebSocket handshake request that the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true send, such as handshake.X-Tenant=acme for an X-Tenant header. The server consumer does not use them. This is a multi-value option with prefix: handshake.

originHeaderUrl.label: security
originHeaderUrl.description: The value of the Origin header of the WebSocket handshake request that the producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true send, such as https://example.com. It is sent even when allowOriginHeader is false. If not set, the Origin is derived from the host and port of the server, unless allowOriginHeader is false.

sslContextParameters.label: security
sslContextParameters.description: The TLS configuration as org.apache.camel.support.jsse.SSLContextParameters. The server consumer accepts wss connections with it, and all consumers on the same host and port must use the same instance or none, otherwise the consumer fails to start. The producer and a consumer with consumeAsClient=true connect with TLS using it. If not set and the useGlobalSslContextParameters option of the component is true, the global SSL context parameters are used.
